overview.purpose: Distributed realtime message processing platform designed to operate at scale, handling billions of messages per day across decentralized topologies without single points of failure.
overview.architectureType: Decentralized daemon-based message queue (nsqd) with in-memory Go channels backed by bounded diskqueue spilling, client-driven RDY flow control, probabilistic priority-queue timeout sweepers, and independent discovery nodes (nsqlookupd).
keyDifferentiators: Zero-broker centralized coordination: nsqd nodes operate completely autonomously without peer-to-peer data replication or single points of failure
Seamless memory-to-disk spilling: high-throughput in-memory channels automatically spill to go-diskqueue files without blocking publishing clients when capacity is reached
Push-based streaming with client-managed backpressure: consumers dictate batch sizes via RDY count updates, eliminating polling overhead while preventing consumer buffer saturation
Probabilistic Redis-style queue scanner: worker pool periodically samples random channels for expired in-flight and deferred messages, dynamically looping without sleep under heavy workload bursts
Independent discovery mesh via nsqlookupd: consumers query stateless lookup daemons for topic producers and establish direct TCP connections to all relevant nsqd daemons

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: TCP Server Shutdown Deadlock from Idle Clients Connecting Without Protocol Magic
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: TCPServer accepted raw TCP socket and incremented WaitGroup, but tcpServer.Handle only registered the connection in conns map after reading 4-byte magic via io.ReadFull without pre-set deadline.
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Track accepted raw sockets in pendingConns sync.Map immediately upon Accept(); iterate and close both conns and pendingConns in tcpServer.Close().

sourceEvidence.observation: p.pendingConns.Store(conn.RemoteAddr(), conn) is called before io.ReadFull, and p.pendingConns.Delete is called once handshake completes or errors.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: A client opening a TCP connection without sending data caused io.ReadFull to block indefinitely, leaving the connection invisible to Close() and blocking nsqd.Exit() in waitGroup.Wait().
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Added pendingConns map in tcpServer and registered connections before io.ReadFull (commit e9ba0b486844e426918065e897b8a36cca5c6aaf, test in tcp_test.go).

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Always register newly accepted network connections into active tracking collections before initiating blocking read handshakes.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Ephemeral Channel Live-Lock Race Condition During Consumer Subscription and Topic Deletion
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: When the last consumer disconnected from an ephemeral channel, channel deletion ran asynchronously; a concurrent SUB command could retrieve the channel pointer via GetChannel() before AddClient() failed due to closing state, causing tight retry loops.
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Bound ephemeral SUB retry attempts to maximum 2 iterations with a 100ms backoff sleep before failing fatally with E_SUB_FAILED.

sourceEvidence.observation: protocolV2.SUB executes a retry loop: if (channel.ephemeral && channel.Exiting()), it removes client, sleeps 100ms, and aborts after 2 tries.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Race window between GetChannel() and AddClient() on ephemeral channel being destroyed led to CPU-spinning subscription live-locks.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Added iteration counter (i < 2) and 100ms sleep in protocolV2.SUB (commit 7521c9db979bcdc484816e92b6492d55d946743a).

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Guard dynamic entity creation/lookup with monotonic lifecycle state checks and bounded retry counts.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: DiskQueue Write Failure Due to Filesystem Exhaustion or Permissions Corruption
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: writeMessageToBackend returns non-nil error when backend.Put fails (e.g. ENOSPC or EACCES).
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Record failure in atomic errValue via nsqd.SetHealth(err); log error and immediately return HTTP 500 status on /ping endpoint to alert load balancers and orchestrators.

sourceEvidence.observation: Calls writeMessageToBackend(m, t.backend) and updates daemon health status via t.nsqd.SetHealth(err).

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Disk full or corrupted data directory prevents message persistence on memory queue overflow.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Integrated SetHealth with atomic.Value errValue and exposed in /ping HTTP handler.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Expose degraded health signals immediately through liveness/readiness probes to remove failing brokers from upstream publish pools.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Consumer Stall or GC Pause Exceeding MsgTimeout Causing Dual Delivery
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: queueScanWorker inspects inFlightPQ priority heap; when currentTime >= msg.pri, message lease is deemed expired.
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Pop message from inFlightMessages, increment channel timeoutCount, notify client via TimedOutMessage() to decrement inFlightCount, and requeue message via Channel.put().

sourceEvidence.observation: processInFlightQueue pops expired items from inFlightPQ, notifies client, and re-inserts message into channel queue.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Slow consumers or network partitions cause message visibility timeout expiration while worker is still processing.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Implemented TOUCH command allowing consumers to dynamically reset msg.pri up to MaxMsgTimeout.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Consumers must periodically send TOUCH heartbeats for long-running jobs and make message processing handlers strictly idempotent.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: NTP Clock Step Backwards Breaking GUID Monotonicity
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Reject GUID generation with ErrTimeBackwards; Topic.GenerateID retries once per millisecond while logging error every 10,000 attempts until clock catches up.

sourceEvidence.observation: guidFactory.NewGUID returns ErrTimeBackwards when current timestamp is less than lastTimestamp.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: NTP backward clock adjustments or leap seconds cause non-monotonic snowflake ID collisions.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Added ErrTimeBackwards guard and retry loop in Topic.GenerateID (topic.go:L500-L513).

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Use monotonic clock primitives or halt ID generation until wall clock exceeds previously recorded high-water mark.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Output Buffer Timeout Misconfiguration Causing Client Connection Starvation
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: Client specifying excessively low or high output_buffer_timeout in IDENTIFY payload.
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Enforce strict boundary validation in SetOutputBuffer: clamp timeout between MinOutputBufferTimeout (25ms) and MaxOutputBufferTimeout (30s).

sourceEvidence.observation: Validates desiredTimeout against MinOutputBufferTimeout and MaxOutputBufferTimeout options.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Unbounded client output buffer timeouts caused high CPU overhead on nsqd when set too small, or excessive delivery latency when set too large.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Enforce strict server-side upper and lower bounds on all client-negotiable timeout and buffer parameters.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: TCP Shutdown Deadlock from Pre-Handshake Client Connections
historicalEvolution.rootCause: TCPServer counted incoming connections in WaitGroup upon Accept(), but Handle() only stored connections in conns map after io.ReadFull finished reading 4-byte magic. Clients that connected and sent nothing blocked nsqd.Exit() forever.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Introduced pendingConns sync.Map to track raw net.Conn objects immediately upon acceptance and updated tcpServer.Close() to iterate and close both conns and pendingConns.

evidence.observation: p.pendingConns.Store(conn.RemoteAddr(), conn) registers connection before io.ReadFull.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Ephemeral Channel Subscription Live-Lock Race Fix
historicalEvolution.rootCause: Concurrent SUB request retrieved closing ephemeral channel from GetChannel() before AddClient() failed, triggering infinite spinning retry loops.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Added bounded retry loop (maximum 2 iterations) with 100ms backoff sleep in protocolV2.SUB before terminating with fatal client error.

evidence.observation: Iterates retry loop with time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond) when subscribing to exiting ephemeral topic/channel.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Zero Memory Queue Size Configuration for Strict Disk-Only FIFO Ordering
historicalEvolution.rootCause: When --mem-queue-size=0 was configured, memoryMsgChan was still allocated with buffer 0, causing non-deterministic select interleaving between unbuffered channel and diskqueue.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Set memoryMsgChan = nil when mem-queue-size == 0 (unless ephemeral), ensuring topic and channel message pumps only select from backend diskqueue for strict sequential ordering.

evidence.observation: Only initializes memoryMsgChan if MemQueueSize > 0 or c.ephemeral is true.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Enforcement of Min and Max Output Buffer Timeouts
historicalEvolution.rootCause: Clients could request arbitrarily small output buffer timeouts, placing heavy scheduling load on runtime tickers and degrading throughput.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Added --min-output-buffer-timeout option (default 25ms) and clamped requested client buffer timeouts within [MinOutputBufferTimeout, MaxOutputBufferTimeout].

evidence.observation: SetOutputBuffer validates desiredTimeout against MinOutputBufferTimeout and MaxOutputBufferTimeout options.

historicalEvolution.rootCause: Closing topics only closed consumer connections attached to channels, leaving pure publish (producer) TCP connections open and causing nsqd.Exit() to stall in waitGroup.Wait().
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Added tcpServer.Close() to explicitly iterate all client connections and terminate producer sockets upon daemon exit.

evidence.observation: NSQD.Exit calls n.tcpServer.Close() before closing topics and waiting on waitGroup.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: Messages are delivered with at-least-once reliability to subscribed channels.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: Ungraceful process termination (SIGKILL, host power failure, OOM) before backend diskqueue sync (governed by SyncEvery count and SyncTimeout interval) causes in-memory messages in memoryMsgChan and un-fsynced disk segments to be permanently lost without recovery.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: diskqueue is instantiated with SyncEvery and SyncTimeout parameters; writes to memoryMsgChan and un-synced OS page cache are not durable until fsync occurs or graceful exit flush() executes.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: A message is leased exclusively to one consumer during its in-flight processing window.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: If a consumer encounters a network partition or prolonged GC pause exceeding MsgTimeout without sending TOUCH, queueScanWorker evicts the lease and requeues the message. A second consumer dequeues and executes the task concurrently with the original stalled worker. When the first worker finishes, its FIN is rejected with E_FIN_FAILED, but duplicate business execution has already occurred.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: processInFlightQueue removes the message from inFlightMessages map upon timeout. Subsequent FIN from the original client fails popInFlightMessage with 'ID not in flight'.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: Topic messages preserve FIFO publication order when delivered to channels.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: When memoryMsgChan is filled to capacity, new messages spill into diskqueue. As consumers drain messages, the messagePump selects concurrently across memoryMsgChan and backend.ReadChan(); messages stored in memory are delivered ahead of older messages that spilled to diskqueue during peak load.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: Go select statement between memoryMsgChan and backendChan exhibits pseudo-random selection semantics when both channels have ready items, violating global FIFO ordering.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: In-flight message timeouts are reclaimed promptly at expiration.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: queueScanLoop uses probabilistic sampling (selecting 20 random channels every 100ms). When a cluster hosts thousands of channels with sparse message traffic, an expired in-flight message in an unselected channel can remain un-requeued for several seconds past its exact expiration deadline.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: queueScanLoop only samples num = QueueScanSelectionCount (20) channels per tick; channels outside the random sample are not checked until selected in subsequent ticks.

boundaryConditions: Process crash or power failure prior to diskqueue SyncTimeout/SyncEvery leads to silent loss of up to MemQueueSize messages in memory plus un-synced disk write buffers.
NTP backward clock adjustments exceeding 0 milliseconds cause guidFactory to reject ID generation (ErrTimeBackwards), blocking publisher PutMessage calls in 1ms retry loops.
High channel cardinalities (10,000+ channels) dilute the 20-channel probabilistic scanner, causing expired message reclamation latency to stretch far beyond QueueScanInterval.
Ephemeral channels experiencing abrupt client disconnection during heavy publishing bursts can drop pending messages if deleter runs before messagePump drains.
untestedAssumptions: Assumes consumers are strictly idempotent and capable of safely processing duplicate message deliveries resulting from network stalls or timeout sweeps.
Assumes local filesystem write latency on DataPath is bounded and will not block writeMessageToBackend or dirlock operations.
Assumes client network partitions do not outlive HeartbeatInterval * 2 read deadlines.
Assumes consumer applications gracefully handle TCP reset frames upon daemon shutdown rather than expecting server-side message reassignment.
acceptedTradeOffs: At-least-once delivery over strict exactly-once processing: eliminates distributed transactions, 2PC, and Raft consensus overhead in exchange for high single-node throughput.
Probabilistic channel scanning over global timer heaps: avoids centralized lock contention across all topics/channels at the expense of non-deterministic eviction timing.
Non-blocking memory spilling over publisher backpressure: ensures publishing clients never block on consumer slow-downs, trading strict FIFO ordering during overflow for uninterrupted ingestion.
Independent decentralized discovery (nsqlookupd) over strong metadata consensus: provides eventual consistency across cluster nodes without Paxos/Zookeeper operational complexity.
